\caption{\small Page recall by scan class, for every retriever and depth. The embedded text layer is near-absent on a scanned page, so the three retrievers that rank it recover almost nothing there; ranking the parser's markdown instead restores most of it, and ranking the page image makes the distinction disappear.}

% {\footnotesize\raggedright
% Page-level recall (\%) against the annotated evidence pages, at retrieval depths
% $k \in \{1,3,5,7,10\}$, rendered at 200 DPI on the MMLongBench-Doc answerable pool
% ($n{=}847$, split 657 born-digital and 190 scanned). Teal deepens with recall on one scale
% shared by both halves, so a scanned cell reads against a born-digital one; bold is the best
% retriever in its own channel at that depth and scan class.
% \textbf{Recall and not precision, by construction.} A single arm at depth $k$ returns exactly
% $k$ pages, so its precision is its recall times $g/k$ and a precision column would be a
% rescaled copy of this one. The joint arms are not here either: a union of a text and a vision
% arm belongs to no one channel.
% \textbf{The scan split is \texttt{annotations/auto\_scan.csv} by document}, which is derived
% from the PDFs and covers every one of them, rather than the generation-time
% \texttt{scan\_label} the parser tables split on. A retrieval row carries no
% \texttt{scan\_label} at all, and the two disagree on 11 questions, which is why this table's
% 657/190 is not the parser table's 646/201.
% \textbf{The embedded-text channel does not degrade on scans, it stops ranking altogether.}
% Its three retrievers read 2.5\% at $k{=}1$ and are still under 30\% at $k{=}10$, and the stored
% rankings say why: on the 190 scanned questions BM25 and Qwen3-Embedding return an identical
% page order on 189 of them, and BM25's ranking is literally $1, 2, 3, \dots$ on 185. On the
% born-digital half the same two agree on 8 of 657. So the 2.5\% is not a weak ranking, it is the
% rate at which the gold page happens to be page one. \textbf{The parser
% recovers most of it}: the same three rungs over PaddleOCR-VL's markdown read 22.5 to 35.2\% at
% $k{=}1$ and 59.3 to 67.5\% at $k{=}10$, within a few points of their own born-digital numbers.
% \textbf{The page image is indifferent to the distinction} and leads on both halves at every
% depth, ColQwen3 reaching 54.2/53.7\% at $k{=}1$. So the choice of text channel matters most
% exactly where the corpus is hardest, and the page image sidesteps the choice.\par}
